# `shipment` commands

## `shipment cancel`

End a draft shipment: it holds nothing any more and never ships. Packing layer.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.cancel` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment cancel 1004 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Not going today" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment cancel", "input": {"shipment": "1004"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

## `shipment create`

Make a draft shipment to pack before it ships: from an order (what `shipment post` would propose), its `lines`, or a `pick_list` (what was picked). Moves and posts nothing; its units are held from other shipments of the order. `packages` boxes it now. Ship it with `shipment post --shipment <number>`. Packing layer: off unless pick_and_pack_enabled (E_FEATURE_DISABLED). Example: {"sales_order": "1001"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment create --sales-order 1001 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Pack before the truck" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment create", "input": {"sales_order": "1001"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `count_position` | `--count-position` | literal["before", "after"] \| null | no | yes | null | Before (the default) or after a physical count of its site on the ship date. |
| `ship_method` | `--ship-method` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Ship Via list entry; default the order's. |
| `carrier` | `--carrier` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Carrier or service, as text. |
| `tracking_numbers` | `--tracking-numbers` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Tracking numbers, recorded and printed as text. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `freight_amount` | `--freight-amount` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Freight to bill, e.g. "12.50": billed once, by the shipment's first invoice; "0" clears it. |
| `freight_item` | `--freight-item` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Other-charge or service item the freight bills as; default the company's shipping item. |
| `sales_order` | `--sales-order` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The order the draft will ship: what `shipment post` would propose, or `lines`; with pick_list, needed only when the list covers several orders. |
| `pick_list` | `--pick-list` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Draft what was picked on this list for the order. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Planned ship date; omitted, the day it ships. |
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `lines[].order_line` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | The order line's line_id (as `sales-order show` lists it). Give this or item. |
| `lines[].item` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | An item exactly one of the order's lines with something to ship carries (name, id or barcode). |
| `lines[].quantity` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | How many to ship, in the order line's unit; omitted, all it has to ship. |
| `lines[].bin` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Bin at the line's site (id, full name A:3 or label code); "(no bin)" is outside every bin. Omitted: the bin the stock stood in, else the item's default bin. |
| `lines[].lot` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Lot an incoming line receives into (made when new) or an outgoing line takes from; omitted, outgoing units leave unassigned. |
| `lines[].serial_numbers` | inside `--lines` JSON array | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Serial numbers, one per unit, up to the quantity; unnumbered units stay unassigned. Never invent one. Omitted on a correction, the line keeps its numbers. |
| `packages[].box` | inside `--packages` JSON array | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Box number; default the next one. |
| `packages[].package_type` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `packages[].weight` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Measured weight, in the company weight unit. |
| `packages[].tare` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Empty package weight, added to the computed weight. |
| `packages[].dimensions` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `packages[].tracking_number` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `packages[].contents[].line` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | The shipment line: its position or line_identity. |
| `packages[].contents[].item` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | An item exactly one line carries. |
| `packages[].contents[].quantity` | inside `--packages` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Base units in the box; omitted, the serials' count or all. |
| `packages[].contents[].serial_numbers` | inside `--packages` JSON array | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | — |

## `shipment invoice`

Invoice one shipment: its units not yet invoiced, at the order's prices, taxed as an ordinary invoice of its own date (default today, never before the ship date). The invoice moves no stock; it moves the units' cost from Shipped Not Invoiced to cost of goods sold. The same as `sales-order invoice <order> --shipments <shipment>`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | ledger.post and customer-work standard role |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Additional resources | customer-work: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.invoice` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment invoice 1001 --date 2026-12-12 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Bill last week's shipment" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment invoice", "input": {"shipment": "1001", "date": "2026-12-12"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shipment` | `SHIPMENT` | string | yes | no | — | Shipment number or id: its units not yet invoiced are billed.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Invoice date, on or after the ship date; default today. |
| `conversion_key` | `--conversion-key` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Retry key: the same key returns the original invoice. Default derived from the shipment. |
| `number` | `--number` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `ar_account` | `--ar-account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `terms` | `--terms` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `apply_prepayment` | `--apply-prepayment` | boolean | no | no | true | Use money held on the order toward the invoice. |

| `settlement.prospective_pages[].request.input.amount` | string \| object \| string \| object \| null | no | no | — | Cash received, 0.00 or more. 0.00 is the anchor's write-off of a bad debt: no cash, every invoice written off named in `discounts` with its expected_version, `discount_account` an expense account such as Bad Debt, and a reason. A write-off may name an inactive customer, posts nothing to the bank and leaves sales tax as it stood. Example: {"customer": "Bauer Builders", "date": "2026-07-31", "amount": "0.00", "operation_key": "wo-1", "discounts": [{"invoice": "2388", "amount": "442.50", "expected_version": 1}], "discount_account": "Bad Debt"}. Preview any of them with dry_run. Present in ReceivePreviewRequest, ApplyPreviewRequest, UnapplyPreviewRequest. |

Present in SuggestedApplications. Present in ReceivePreviewRequest. |
| `settlement.prospective_pages[].request.input.discounts` | array[object] | no | no | [] | Early-payment discounts, one per invoice. The invoice is settled by the cash applied to it (if any) plus the discount; an invoice given no cash here needs its expected_version, and the receipt as a whole records cash received unless it is a write-off (amount 0.00). The discount is debited to the discount account. Never taken unless listed: `payment invoices` shows each invoice's discount date and suggested discount. Example: a 1,000.00 invoice on 2% 10 Net 30 paid in time takes applications {"invoice": "1043", "amount": "980.00", ...} and discounts [{"invoice": "1043", "amount": "20.00"}]. Present in ReceivePreviewRequest. |

Required for a write-off (amount 0.00), where it must be an expense account such as Bad Debt. Present in ReceivePreviewRequest. |
| `settlement.prospective_pages[].request.input.underpayment` | literal["leave_open", "write_off"] | no | no | "leave_open" | What happens when the cash is less than the invoices it pays (the anchor's Receive Payments choice). "leave_open" (default): each invoice keeps what it still owes; `summary.underpayment` says how to write it off later. "write_off": every invoice given cash is paid in full, the short part (after any listed discount) going to `write_off_account` with `write_off_class`. Example: 480.00 applied to a 500.00 invoice with underpayment "write_off", write_off_account "Bad Debt". Present in ReceivePreviewRequest. |

## `shipment pack`

Pack a draft or a shipped shipment; posts nothing. Either the whole packing (`packages`: box, package_type, weight, tare, dimensions, tracking_number, contents by line, item or serial_numbers), or a move: `unit` (a serial number, lot or item code) or `line`, `quantity` (default 1) into `box` N, made if new; box 0 unboxes. With no unit, the facts set box N. A box weighs its contents (item unit weight) plus tare, or its measured weight. Example: {"shipment": "1004", "unit": "WH-1001", "box": 2}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.pack` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment pack 1004 --unit WH-1001 --box 2 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Heater in box 2" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment pack", "input": {"shipment": "1004", "unit": "WH-1001", "box": 2}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| Option | Meaning |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.pack`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

## `shipment post`

Ship a sales order before invoicing it: the units leave stock on the ship date (default today) and their cost waits in Shipped Not Invoiced, an asset, until the invoice moves it to cost of goods sold beside its income. Nothing reaches income or receivables. With no `lines` it ships every order line's quantity still to ship, up to what is available to the order (on hand less what other orders commit); the rest stays backordered on the order. `lines` name an order line (`order_line`, its line_id) or an `item`, a `quantity` in the order line's unit, and optionally `bin`, `lot` and `serial_numbers`; shipping past what is on hand is allowed with a warning, costed provisionally until the receipt arrives. Carrier and tracking numbers are recorded as text. The dry run shows each line's cost and what stays to ship. The result gives the next command, `shipment invoice <number>`. `pick_list` ships what was picked on it instead; `shipment` posts a draft. `invoice: true` also invoices it in the same transaction. `freight_amount` (and `freight_item`) is billed once, by its first invoice. Example: {"sales_order": "1001"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Additional resources | customer-work: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.post` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment post --sales-order 1001 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Shipped Acme's order" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json

```

## `shipment return`

Record units a customer sent back from a shipment before they were invoiced: they go back into stock on the return date (default today, never before the ship date), to the bin the shipment took them from unless a line names one, worth their share of the shipment line's cost, which leaves Shipped Not Invoiced. `reopen` (default true) leaves them to ship again on the order; false cancels them on it. `lines` name a shipment line (its position or line_identity) or an item, a quantity in the item's base unit, and serial numbers or a lot the shipment took; omitted, every unit still out and not invoiced comes back. Units an invoice billed come back on a credit memo naming the invoice line instead. Example: {"shipment": "1001", "lines": [{"shipment_line": "1", "quantity": "1"}]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Additional resources | customer-work: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.return` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment return 1001 --lines '[{"shipment_line": "1", "quantity": "1"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Acme sent one back before we billed it" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment return", "input": {"shipment": "1001", "lines": [{"shipment_line": "1", "quantity": "1"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shipment` | `SHIPMENT` | string | yes | no | — | Shipment number or id whose units came back.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | The shipment's version, if you want it checked. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Date the units came back into stock; default today, never before the ship date. |
| `lines[].shipment_line` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | The shipment line given back: its position (1, 2, ...) or line_identity, as `shipment show` lists them. Give this or item. |
| `lines[].item` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | An item exactly one line of the shipment carries. |
| `lines[].quantity` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | How many came back, in the item's base unit (as the shipment shows it); omitted, all of the line still out and not invoiced. |
| `lines[].bin` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Bin the units go back to; default the bin the shipment took them from. |
| `lines[].lot` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Lot an incoming line receives into (made when new) or an outgoing line takes from; omitted, outgoing units leave unassigned. |
| `lines[].serial_numbers` | inside `--lines` JSON array | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Serial numbers that came back; each must be one the shipment took. |
| `reopen` | `--reopen` | boolean | no | no | true | True (the default): the units are to ship again on the order. False: they are cancelled on the order. |
| `count_position` | `--count-position` | literal["before", "after"] \| null | no | yes | null | Before (the default) or after a physical count of the site on the return date. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

## `shipment update`

Correct a shipment: its date, count position, lines (replacing them), ship method, carrier, tracking numbers or memo. A change of quantity, place or date reposts the stock at the ship date; a change of ship method, carrier, tracking or memo alone writes a new revision and reposts nothing. Refused below what invoices billed, later than an invoice billing it, or (for a repost) while a return gives back its units -- to take units off a shipment, record a return with `shipment return`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Additional resources | customer-work: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/shipment.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow shipment update 1001 --expected-version 1 --tracking-numbers '["1Z999"]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Tracking from the carrier" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "shipment update", "input": {"shipment": "1001", "expected_version": 1, "tracking_numbers": ["1Z999"]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| `freight_item` | `--freight-item` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Other-charge or service item the freight bills as; default the company's shipping item. |

## `shipment void`

Void a shipment with a reason: its units go back where they left from at the ship date and the order has them to ship again. Refused while an invoice bills it or a return gives back its units, naming them; void or correct those first.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INACTIVE_REFERENCE` | A new or changed reference must name an active record. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERIOD_CLOSED` | An affected accounting date is in a closed period. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VALUE_RANGE` | The value is outside its allowed range or storage bounds. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
| `E_WORK_DEPENDENCY` | The accepted or linked work prevents this change; inspect the related document. |
